record.question: Under the Parquet Scribe settings, whose windows pay for the staging and publication they cause, what does each native, OTLP spans, and OTLP logs write cost the server per CPU-second and per provisioned vCPU at 1 and 64 closed-loop clients up to its durable acknowledgement, with no error, how much publication ran and what backlog remained, and do the native and OTLP write peaks clear their sanity floors?

fixture.native: native-2m: events rows into bifrost.datasets.events_ingest, 2000000 rows per day, fresh ids every window
fixture.spans: spans-2m: GenAI/HTTP spans into bifrost.traces.spans, 2000000 spans per day, fresh ids every window
fixture.spans_1k: spans-1k-2m: the spans-2m spans at about 1 KiB of OTLP wire each (Kubernetes and SDK resource attributes, twelve more span attributes, a prompt and a log event per span) into bifrost.traces.spans, 2000000 spans per day, ids distinct from spans-2m, fresh ids every window
fixture.logs: logs-2m: bulky Kubernetes logs into bifrost.logs.records, 2000000 records per day, fresh ids every window

values.limits: server defaults on the whole host except WYRD_MAX_FILE_RETENTION_TIME=30; no resource quota

timing.recorder: wyrd-benchmark is the server's only metrics recorder: counters, gauges, and diagnostic histograms are read from the same snapshots as the timings, with no Prometheus recorder or exporter; a duration with both a timing and a production histogram is recorded only as the timing
timing.method: server benchmark histograms: integer nanoseconds from the owning server boundary's std::time::Instant timers, recorded into bounded HDR histograms and read as cumulative snapshots from the loopback metrics listener; each window is the bucket-count difference of two snapshots of one process
timing.precision: 3 significant digits; each percentile is judged on its whole bucket's bounds
timing.metric_histograms: fixed-point billionths: a _seconds histogram in range_ns, any other in [1, 4611686018427387904] billionths of its value, so fractional ratios and decimal costs keep their value
timing.percentile: nearest rank ceil(q * N) over the window's distribution
timing.tracing: operator span export stays at its default (disabled); no span is required for timing
timing.assignment: every request carries its closed case and the repetition or admission phase that admitted it, attached when its request span opens; a window takes the observations recorded between its opening snapshot and one taken after its admitted cohort drained, so a late completion stays in its admitted cohort; each cohort's judged-outcome count must equal the completions the driver saw, other outcomes (retried or refused attempts) are counted beside it; a short or extra count, a dropped or out-of-range observation, an unknown label, a missing or negative component, scans that are not the answered cohort's, or a replaced process makes it invalid
timing.measurement: work, wall seconds, and server and driver CPU stop at the admission stop, before the requests then in flight drain; their completions count as late work beside the measured work, and their latency stays in the final cohort
timing.evidence: each window's full opening and drained snapshots are kept under the run's target artifacts as timings/<step>/<phase>.json; the record keeps each cohort's reconciliation and each percentile's rank and bucket bounds

values.workload: closed-loop public-client clients, each sending its next request once the last is acknowledged: native `write_batch` of 16,384 rows; OTLP exports of 512 spans or log records with the client's exchanged bearer
